replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed threats against this design:

- Automated abuse (brute force, mass sign-up, email/SMS flooding, scraping): design is only "Microservices authenticate each other with JWTs" with exposure "internal" — no sign-in form, no notification send, no public page or API returning data. Not applicable.
- Staff/admin/moderator screens rendering user-supplied content: nothing in the design describes any UI, file or profile field. Not applicable.
- Privileged actions (delete, refund, role change, money) with no record of who did it: the design states "signed using a shared HS256 secret that is stored in each service's environment variables", meaning a signature identifies the fleet, not the caller — attribution of internal calls is unachievable. Not covered by the three agreed threats (none is Repudiation).
- Personal/financial documents cacheable by browsers, proxies or CDNs: no document or page described. Not applicable.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV/exports, emails, headers, other interpreters: no such data flow stated. Not applicable.
- Unconfirmed-only items: env-var leak and offline brute force rest on unstated build details or are consequences of agreed threat 1 (secret = signing key); audience/scope replay collapses into agreed threat 1; rotation outage depends on how deploys are built. Only the attribution/repudiation item is real and not covered.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-06",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["microservices", "JWT issuer/verifier", "service environment config"],
    "dataStores": [],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["service-to-service internal API boundary"],
    "dataClasses": ["secrets"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Internal calls cannot be attributed to a specific service, so abuse goes unseen and can be denied",
      "scenario": "Every service signs with the same secret, so a token claiming to be any service is indistinguishable from one minted by any other service or by an attacker holding the secret. A service owner (or an insider operating one service) can call sensitive internal APIs while presenting another service's identity; afterwards logs showing the caller identity prove nothing. Incident responders cannot determine which service or person made a call, and the responsible party can plausibly deny it, so misuse of internal APIs goes undetected and unattributable.",
      "component": "JWT issuance/verification across microservices",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "medium", "reach": "all", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Microservices authenticate each other with JWTs signed using a shared HS256 secret that is stored in each service’s environment variables." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because all services share one signing key, a signed request only proves it came from somewhere inside the system — not which service, so misuse can't be traced or proven.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Attributable service identity and audit of internal calls",
        "given": "an internal service-to-service call authenticated by a JWT",
        "when": "the call reaches a service and is authorised",
        "then": "the caller identity is bound to a per-service credential (distinct key or asymmetric key with key id) and the verified caller, token id and action are recorded in an append-only audit log so the call can be attributed to one service after the fact"
      }
    }
  ]
}
